key_highlights: ASX treads water amid persistent interest rate fears; RBA Governor Bullock's hawkish stance reinforces higher-for-longer narrative
Iron ore downside risk persists, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX near-term
Sydney housing market under severe stress with auction reality check; diesel/petrol price shock adds inflationary pressure
US markets rally (Dow +450pts) on falling oil and Treasury yields; Trump-Xi summit anticipation lifts risk appetite
WA/SA gold exploration pipeline strong: Platina, Broken Hill, Great Southern, Forrestania, Larvotto all advancing projects
Super contributions surge >33% post-budget tax changes, boosting super fund AUM and financials sector
China economic cracks under Xi add external demand risk for Australian commodity exporters
Intergenerational Report questioned on productivity growth assumptions, raising long-term fiscal concerns

sectors.trend: Iron ore downside risk weighs on major miners; gold exploration active across WA/SA with multiple positive drill results; rare earths (Dalaroo) and antimony (Larvotto) diversifying pipeline
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face headwinds from weak iron ore; gold juniors (PLA.AX, BHL.AX, GSO.AX, FRA.AX, LRV.AX) and DLR.AX offer speculative upside; China demand weakness a key risk

sectors.trend: Higher-for-longer rate environment supports NIM but housing stress (Sydney bloodbath, auction reality check) threatens credit quality; super contribution surge boosts fund flows
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from rate tailwind but face rising NPL risk in residential; super funds (HUB.AX, PPA.AX) see AUM tailwind from 33%+ contribution surge

sectors.trend: Diesel and petrol price shock rising; EV adoption accelerating as consumers flee bowser; oil prices falling globally
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WES.AX face margin pressure from fuel cost pass-through; EV transition benefits consumer discretionary; global oil weakness pressures Woodside (WDS.AX) upstream

sectors.trend: US tech strong (Nvidia extends gains, Broadcom defends targets) but Gundlach warns to avoid AI stocks; AI-driven broker disruption noted
sectors.implications: Limited direct ASX exposure; CSL.AX biotech and SVA.AX, W1.AX (software) may benefit from global tech sentiment; caution on AI concentration risk

sectors.trend: Sydney housing bloodbath and auction reality check signal cooling; rental market disruption from agent-bypass platforms; higher rates pressure valuations
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, DGL.AX, ICV.AX) face occupancy and yield pressure; residential property developers under stress

key_themes: Higher-for-longer RBA policy with Bullock hawkish bias
Iron ore structural downside vs. gold/rare earths exploration boom
Housing market correction in Sydney with credit risk implications
China demand fragility as external risk to commodity exporters
Super system reform driving financial flows
Energy transition: fuel cost shock vs. EV adoption
US-China summit (Trump-Xi) as global risk catalyst

risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge rate exposure via bond ladders; favour fixed-income and dividend aristocrats; monitor Bullock commentary

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Iron ore price decline / China demand weakness
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce BHP.AX/RIO.AX/FMG.AX weightings; rotate into gold and critical minerals exposure
Underweight residential REITs and property developers; monitor bank NPL data; favour defensive financials
Favour energy producers with hedged exposure; avoid high-input-cost consumer names

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Geopolitical: Trump-Xi summit / trade war escalation
risk_assessment.mitigation: Diversify away from China-exposed miners; hold quality global equities; monitor AUD/USD
Favour companies with strong pricing power; avoid over-leveraged government-dependent sectors

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold and critical minerals exploration names
opportunities.rationale: Multiple positive WA/SA drill results; gold as inflation/rate hedge; rare earths strategic demand

opportunities.recommendation: Add quality dividend payers in financials on rate tailwind
opportunities.rationale: Higher-for-longer supports NIM; super contribution surge boosts fund AUM; CBA/NAB best positioned

opportunities.recommendation: Selective energy exposure on fuel cost shock
opportunities.rationale: Diesel/petrol price spike benefits integrated producers; EV transition is structural tailwind

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce iron ore major exposure; hedge with gold
defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore downside risk confirmed; China cracks add demand uncertainty; gold provides inverse hedge

defensive_moves.recommendation: Underweight Sydney residential REITs and property developers
defensive_moves.rationale: Housing bloodbath and auction reality check signal deteriorating fundamentals; rate pressure on valuations

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain cash/short-duration bonds as rate uncertainty persists
defensive_moves.rationale: ASX treading water; Bullock hawkish; avoid over-committing equity ahead of RBA guidance

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely range-bound to slightly lower over 1-3 months. Rate fears, housing stress, and iron ore weakness cap upside. US strength (Dow +450) and Trump-Xi summit offer intermittent relief. Expect volatility around RBA commentary and CPI data.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautiously constructive if iron ore stabilises and housing finds floor. Gold/critical minerals pipeline and super reform provide structural support. Key risk: China demand collapse or RBA forced into aggressive tightening. Intergenerational fiscal concerns warrant caution on government-linked sectors.
